MGMT 1110.title: Introduction to Management
MGMT 1110.description: This course provides students with a systematic approach to acquiring a solid foundation in the principles and current practices of management. The focus of the course is about the interaction between individuals (managers) and the organization. We will explore what managers do through discussion of the four fundamental functions of managers, namely planning, organizing, leading and controlling. Topics include: evolution of management theories, environmental influences on management, organizational culture, strategic management, organizational design, change management, organizational control and human resources management.
cilos: Explain what management is and what managers do
Analyze global and task environmental influences on management
Practice ethical management behaviors through an understanding of ethical dilemmas in management issues

Develop basic management skills with respect to:
- Analyze strategic management issues (planning function)
- Evaluate the impact of various organizational designs (organizing function)
- Apply leadership concepts in managing organizational change (leading function)
- Evaluate the effectiveness of organizational control systems (controlling function)

MGMT 1120.title: Developing the Leader in You
MGMT 1120.description: Leading people effectively is a tremendous challenge, a great opportunity, and a serious responsibility.  This course is about developing your full potential as a leader.  The focus will be on skills development so that you can use leadership theories and concepts to improve your leadership skills.  Topics include leadership traits and behavior theories, leadership values, the team concept and group dynamics and leader as coach and developer of people.  Interactive class activities will be conducted including videos, discussions and self-assessment exercises.
cilos: Identify and discuss the power and pitfalls of leadership
Explain the power of leadership with reference to different leadership styles, which includes Legitimate, Coercive, Referent, Charisma, Expert, Information, Reward, Moral, Connection and Founder
Identify and explain with justifications about your leadership style
Apply your leadership style across various situations where time, resources and knowledge is limited
Practice ethical behaviors through an understanding of ethical dilemmas

MGMT 1130.title: Traps and Pitfalls in Judgment and Decision Making
MGMT 1130.description: Decision making is a central human activity, but how good are we at it? Scientific evidence suggests that our decisions are often biased and flawed, resulting in disappointing or even disastrous outcomes. This course draws upon contemporary research in psychology and other social sciences to better understand how it is that people make decisions, and why those decisions are often made badly. The course will emphasize a theoretical understanding of human decision making, as well as a comprehension of the real world implications of our mistakes both for us and for our society, and what, if anything, can be done about it.
cilos: Describe major limits of human cognition that cause errors in judgment and decision-making
Describe major biases in judgment and decision-making, and explain the psychological mechanisms underlying those biases
Discuss the real world implications of our judgment and decision biases for us and for our society, and suggest what can be done to steer people toward better decisions
Work effectively in a team
Communicate ideas persuasively and professionally

MGMT 2010.title: Business Ethics and the Individual
MGMT 2010.description: This course presents and exemplifies three major traditions of ethical thought in East and West moral philosophy - namely utilitarianism, principle-based ethics and virtue-based ethics. Employing guest speakers, lectures, cases, contemporary readings, role-plays, fieldwork, reflective student writing, and discussion groups, the course engages students in a serious consideration of their own ethical standards as applied to their present academic environment and their future careers. Students come to understand through this course that while an ethical dilemma may be viewed in various ways depending on one's guiding assumptions, a decision and course of action nevertheless must be chosen in harmony with one's own moral convictions. For Business students only.
cilos: Understand core concepts and principles of business ethics as applied to contexts with which students are most familiar, including academic integrity.
Describe and practice a logical course of decision-making for reaching ethical conclusions.
Indentify and describe ethical problems and opportunities involved in academic and business life.
Understand and prioritize complementary and conflicting ethical points of view.
Provide succinct summaries of central schools of ethical thought.
Make progress in coming to a personal set of ethical principles to be applied in their study and career.
Appreciate and promulgate the necessity for ethical behavior and leadership to academic and business enterprise at all levels.
Write about and discuss ethical issues cogently and persuasively with internal and external audiences.

MGMT 2011.title: New Venture Creation
MGMT 2011.description: This course introduces students to the fundamental knowledge, mindset, and skill sets required to create and manage new ventures. Through a combination of theory, practical exercises, case studies, and projects, students will learn to recognise, assess, and articulate new opportunities for entrepreneurial ventures, generate innovative business ideas based on technological concepts, and understand the resources and strategies necessary for implementation. Students will be exposed to the real-world challenges of creating a new technical venture and will acquire the essential knowledge and skills for setting up and managing a venture. The course also help participants develop a greater awareness of their personal goals, strengths and limitations in venture creation and growth. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course.
cilos: Understand the process of designing a new venture concept from a technical idea and developing innovative business model for implementation.
Develop practical strategies for identifying, evaluating, and exploiting business opportunity.
Understand the process and acquire fundamental knowledge and skillset in creating a new venture, developing viable business models, and making business plan.
Effectively communicate and articulate the value proposition of a new venture to investors, stakeholders, and decision makers.
Demonstrate foundational business literacy to evaluate the resource required for implementing the designed concept and business model.

MGMT 2110.title: Organizational Behavior
MGMT 2110.description: Human behavior and behavioral issues in organizations studied from the perspective of the individual and that of the organization.
cilos: Demonstrate your understanding of major concepts and theories in OB.

Analyze management issues at the individual, team and organizational levels critically and creatively. 
a. Being critical refers to the application of OB theories to solving organizational problems in a manner that shows your awareness of (i) exactly how the theory of your choice applies to the issue being analyzed and (ii) the risks and benefits associated with each solution suggested. 
b. Being creative refers to finding solutions to management issues not necessarily referred to in your textbook, as long as such solutions are theoretically justified.
Apply concepts and theories in OB learned in this course to solve business problems.
Communicate and present your ideas clearly, persuasively, and professionally (through writing, presentations, and discussions).
Enhance your personal ability to function effectively in a multicultural settings.
Develop an understanding of personal strengths and weaknesses in organizational contexts.

MGMT 2130.title: Business Ethics and Social Responsibility
MGMT 2130.description: Taking a discussion-based approach to examining ethical issues in a corporate context, this intermediate business ethics course will focus mainly on the ethical issues related to the interaction between business and society. Students will further develop their ethical knowledge, moral reasoning skills, and attitudes towards social responsibility by considering the overarching corporate implications of their decisions. This highly interactive course will draw upon relevant current issues to help students understand (and overcome) some of the real-world challenges that business executives confront.
MGMT 2130.prerequisite: (for non-BIBU, non-RMBI and non-SGFN students) MGMT 2010
cilos: Understand concepts / terminology associated with business ethics and social responsibility.
Know the basic principles of ethical decision-making and Stakeholder Management.
Identify ethical dilemmas in business.
Analyze arid propose solutions to business challenges involving moral ambiguity.
Appreciate the importance of behaving ethically in society.
Gain an awareness of one's professional and ethical responsibility in society.

MGMT 3110.title: Human Resources Management
MGMT 3110.description: Manpower planning, job analysis and design, recruitment, performance appraisal, compensation, training and development, health and safety at work and discrimination.
cilos: Explain, compare, and contrast, and apply basic HRM concepts, techniques and industrial practices.
Critically analyze HRM issues in real organizations, develop, and defend reasoned solutions with sound theoretical viewpoints.

MGMT 3120.title: Managerial Leadership
MGMT 3120.description: Understand the nature of leadership and how it goes beyond managership. To develop an appreciation for the complexities of dealing with people who hold different values. To introduce, develop and encourage new strategies and techniques to enhance both teamwork and effectiveness in the workplace.
cilos: Demonstrate understanding of key leadership theories and concepts.
Apply leadership theories critically to analyze and address real-world challenges.
Reflect on personal leadership development and cultivate leadership skills to navigate complex, fast-changing professional contexts.

MGMT 3130.title: Judgement and Decision Making in Organizations
MGMT 3130.description: This course is about how people make decisions, with special emphasis on decision making in an organizational context. It attempts to provide an understanding of employee and manager decision making at two levels - the individual and the group.
cilos: Explain why decision making is an important component in managing organizations.

Describe various biases in individual decision making and group decision making.
Apply theories related to judgment and decision making in organization-relevant domains such as human resources management, marketing, entrepreneurship, and ethics.
Develop skills for effective teamwork.
Develop skills for effective communication.

MGMT 3140.title: Negotiation
MGMT 3140.description: Theories and processes of negotiation; negotiation strategies; contextual factors in negotiation; other issues in negotiation.
cilos: Understand the core negotiation concepts and the situations where they apply. This will involve leaning how to compare, contrast, and differentiate among negotiation situations.
Develop greater confidence when negotiating.
Demonstrate the ability to understand and predict the behavior and motives of individuals and groups across negotiation situations.
Critically analyze negotiation situations to identify where they can be applied versus where they need to be modified.
Demonstarte the ability to design and implement strategies for negotiating effectively across a wide range of contexts, including novel situations.

MGMT 3160.title: Environmental Business Strategies
MGMT 3160.description: This course covers strategic opportunities arising from environmental risks. Public and regulatory demand for environmental products and services must co-exist with the need for corporations to maximize shareholder wealth. The course examines both theoretical and practical issues that arise in attempting to balance the health of the natural environment with value creation. Is there an inherent conflict between the institutions of business and our ability to care for the environment? What competitive opportunities are created for firms and what do they have to do to seize these opportunities? Lessons from the course will be interest to the students of strategy and the environment. Restricted to MGMT and BBA students.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the conceptual relationships between environmental impacts and a firm's business strategy.
Assess the efficacy of the incorporation of environmental perspectives into the design of competitive strategies.
Analyze business situations to identify alternative environmental strategies and recommend environmentally responsible solutions.
Apply an understanding of how environmental issues affect strategic business decisions.
Synthesize an environmentally sustainable business model for a business.
Develop and understanding of how firms can engage in environmental stewardship and practice environmental and social responsibility.
Practice teamwork.

MGMT 3170.title: Managing CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility)
MGMT 3170.description: This course will focus on specific CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) issues facing companies today. Along with changing attitudes, new global regulatory CSR requirements are increasingly putting firms under pressure to demonstrate positive social and environmental impacts, while maintaining their commitments to investors. Students will investigate how actual firms are managing these pressures while continuing to address the needs of their stakeholders. Incorporating aspects of the benchmark standards such as the GRI and various ESG (Environmental Social Governance) initiatives will help students to strengthen their own knowledge, skill, and attitudes in this area. The course has an embedded project, with direct links to one or more businesses, which will give students the necessary practical grounding for effectively understanding the challenges of CSR in the contemporary business environment.
cilos: Understand concepts / terminology associated with CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility).
Understand the need for businesses to address CSR issues.
Identify key value drivers for CSR.
Analyze and propose solutions to help businesses overcome some of the challenges that accompany CSR in terms of its monitoring and reporting.
Appreciate how businesses can develop strategies that incorporate CSR components while ensuring their own commercial viability.
Gain an awareness of the rising expectations from various stakeholders who want to see companies take up their genuine corporate social responsibility.

MGMT 4000.title: Special Topics in Management
MGMT 4000.description: Current development issues in the field of organization and management; topics selected by instructors.

MGMT 4210.title: Corporate Strategy

MGMT 4220.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
MGMT 4220.description: This is an interactive course that introduces knowledge about the creation and management of new business ventures. Attention is also given to key issues in corporate entrepreneurship, social entrepreneurship, and family businesses.
cilos: Understand the nature of entrepreneurship and entrepreneurial processes.
Recognize and evaluate business opportunities.

Develop fundamental and economic understanding of innovation.

MGMT 4230.title: International Management
MGMT 4230.description: Understanding and managing multinational corporations in different economic, social, cultural, legal and technological environments.
cilos: Explain the nature of competitive advantages and assess the competitiveness of companies in international business.

Apply your knowledge to analyze the international business environment facing a firm, assess the attractiveness of its industry and isolate potential sources of competitive advantages and disadvantages.
Develop solutions designed to build and sustain international competitive advantages.
Develop effective implementation plans while considering the human element of organizations.

MGMT 4240.title: Strategic Management in China
MGMT 4240.description: The overall goal of this course is to teach the students key theories and frameworks in strategic management and apply them to Chinese context.  it takes a comparative perspective to analyze the similarities and differences in strategic management between East and West.  It is case intensive course which involves extensive student participation in analyzing cases of business in China.
cilos: Understand the extent to which China is different from other countries and how such differences affect business strategies in the Chinese context.
Assess the opportunities and challenges of setting up business operations in China, and develop corresponding sound business & corporate strategies.
Design and evaluate recommendations for multinational companies seeking to develop China strategies in order to compete in the Chinese market more successfully.

MGMT 4250.title: Management Consulting
MGMT 4250.description: To meet the increasing demand from both the private and public sectors in local and international firms in Hong Kong, South East Asia and mainland China, Management Consulting is a course to be offered by faculty with consulting experience who will train students in management with the fundamental and practical skills to understand and analyse business problems in order to work out a number of scenarios for solving problems. More importantly, the students will be encouraged to work in teams and propose innovative and strategic consulting plans to meet a set of specified goals from time to time.
cilos: Learn key consulting techniques.
Apply consulting techniques to an actual project and recommend an actionable solution.
Demonstrate mastery by presenting a deck.

MGMT 4270.title: Training and Development
MGMT 4270.description: In today's competitive business world, organizations need to implement training and development initiatives to continuously cultivate their human resources. This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the training and developing process in organizations. Topics include training needs assessment, learning motivation, theories of learning, transfer of training, training methods, and training evaluation. The course will also examine special topics of interest such as cross-cultural training, career development, and the role of information technology and social responsibility in training and development.
cilos: Articulate how training and development contributes to the achievement of organizational goals.
Conduct training needs assessment, and identify training objectives.
Apply various theories of motivation, learning, and transfer to design effective training activities and select training methods.
Evaluate the effectiveness of training programs.
Describe recent trends in training and development such as cross-cultural training, career development, and the role of information technology and social responsibility in training and development.
Develop skills for effective teamwork.
Develop skills for effective communication.

MGMT 4280.title: Transnational Legal Issues and Dispute Settlement
MGMT 4280.description: The course introduces students to core legal principles of transnational economic law with special emphasis on cross-border commercial legal issues, alongside mechanisms for settling trade and investment disputes. Key focus areas include legal challenges in cross-border commercial contracts (choice of law, jurisdiction clauses, force majeure, anti-bribery compliance), arbitration (UNCITRAL, HKIAC), mediation, and ICSID investor-state arbitration. Lectures analyze how domestic laws, WTO agreements, and international conventions impact multinational operations in sectors like energy, infrastructure, and pharmaceuticals. Students learn practical strategies to mitigate risks through robust contract drafting and ADR, drawing from real-world cases like jurisdictional battles and enforcement under the New York Convention.
cilos: Understand why knowing the law is an advantage for a business leader.
Develop an understanding of the laws, regulations, and institutions that govern transnational economic activities.
Develop their knowledge of the core principles of international contract drafting and the settlement of international commercial disputes.
Understand the role of the WTO trade agreements and dispute settlement mechanism.
Develop an understanding of international labour regulations.
Learn the core principles of investor-state arbitration.
Develop their understanding of alternative dispute resolutions mechanism Arbitration and Mediation.
Learn how to do basic legal research.
Acquire skills and knowledge that will expand their career opportunities.

MGMT 4280.title: Transnational Legal Issues and Dispute Settlement
MGMT 4280.description: The course introduces students to core legal principles of transnational economic law and the mechanisms for the settlement of trade and investment disputes. The topics discussed are closely related to world-wide current events that affect transnational law and dispute resolution. The lectures examine how domestic laws, and regional and international agreements impact the operations of corporations in different economic sectors (i.e. energy, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals etc,) and in labour relations. The course covers decisions of international courts and arbitral tribunals that affect the activities and governance of private and state-owned multinational corporations. Students will learn how companies can minimize the impact of problematic situations through arbitration, mediation, and alternative means of dispute settlement. The understanding of key legal concepts that govern cross-border trade and investment ensures a holistic preparation to management and business students and enables them to better address complex issues that companies face in a globalised economy.
cilos: Understand why knowing the law is an advantage for a business leader.
Develop an understanding of the laws, regulations, and institutions that govern transnational economic activities.
Develop their knowledge of the core principles of international contract drafting and the settlement of international commercial disputes.
Understand the role of the WTO trade agreements and dispute settlement mechanism.

MGMT 4290.title: HR Analytics
MGMT 4290.description: HR analytics, also known as “people analytics” and “talent analytics”, is the use of HR data and analytical tools to improve decision making in human resources and ultimately contribute to organizational effectiveness. It is an evidence-based, data-driven approach to managing people at work. In this course, we will examine the HR data and analytical tools necessary to conducting HR analytics, and apply them in resolving HR issues such as recruitment and selection, performance evaluation, training and development, compensation, and retention. We will also discuss the ethical aspects related to HR analytics.
cilos: Articulate how HR analytics contributes to organizational effectiveness, and illustrate with examples in international settings.
Formulate HR problems into research designs that will generate insights for decision making in various HR functions (e.g. recruitment and selection, talent retention).
Analyze HR data using descriptive and predictive analytical techniques, with the help of statistical data analysis software.
Communicate findings and insights generated from HR analytics.
Demonstrate awareness of ethical aspects of collecting and utilizing HR data.
Develop effective teamwork skills for team projects.

MGMT 4300.title: Knowing and Managing Your Social Networks for Careers and Business
MGMT 4300.description: Business environments change, but what stays constant is that business still involves people and relationships. Knowing the right people and building a helpful network of people are critical to successful careers. Throughout this course, you  will learn about: 1)  why are networks important, and how, 2) what are the different  aspects of networks that matter, and 3) how does your network look like? To answer these questions, this course will introduce you to elementary theories of social networks and skills in network science.
cilos: Understand key concepts in network science.
Understand the network drivers of successful careers and business.
Understand the drivers and impediments of building a helpful network.
Understand your own networks and others' networks.
Develop, collect, and analyze network data to uncover and evaluate important aspects of networks.
Effectively communicate ideas in both oral and written form.
Effective collaborate in diverse teams.

MGMT 4310.title: Power, Influence, and Persuasion
MGMT 4310.description: This is an advanced experiential course allowing students to explore and practice the strategies of power and influence experienced in the business world. The course connects scientific theory with relevant practice and focuses on experimenting with specific techniques to achieve desired outcomes in investing, management, and entrepreneurship contexts. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course.
cilos: Understand core concepts related to persuasion, decision making, and behavior.
Use basic concepts in their daily life and have an ability to apply them to a variety of situations.
Understand how people judge one another and the various dimensions and trade-offs involved in how we are judged.
Understand their own persuasive profile and how they are different from others on specific dimensions related to persuasion and influence.

MGMT 5110.title: Managerial Communication
MGMT 5110.description: Communication skill ranks at the top of contributors to job effectiveness, satisfaction and success. Managerial communication gives students an opportunity to improve students' ability to communicate efficiently and effectively as a manager and to develop those critical communication capabilities that students will need as a business leader.
cilos: Communicate more effectively in business environments as managers and leaders.
Continue practicing their communication skills for continuous improvement in the future.

cilos: Communicate more effectively in business environments as managers and leaders.

MGMT 5210.title: Preparing to Lead
MGMT 5210.description: The practical study of managerial work. Examines communication skills and offers the opportunity for assessment and feedback. Organizational contexts, team building and case work. This is a required immersion program for MBA programs. Graded P or F.
cilos: Define the concept of leadership in organizations.
Develop skills and competencies that enable effective leadership.
Develop a plan that will enable an immediate and noticeable impact on how they lead at work.

MGMT 5210.description: The practical study of managerial work. Examines communication skills and offers the opportunity for assessment and feedback. Organizational contexts, team building and case work. This is a required immersion program for MBA programs. Graded P or F.

MGMT 5230.title: Management of Organizations
MGMT 5230.description: Include motivation theories, leadership, group dynamics, job design, decision making, power and politics, organizational structure and design, and organizational change.
cilos: Improve general decision making and managerial decision making.
Lead a team and work within a group.
Motivate and manage others at work.
Negotiate effectively.
Identify ethical challenges in oneself and others.

MGMT 5410.title: Strategic Management
MGMT 5410.description: Major techniques and approaches to the development and implementation of corporate strategies. Underlying concepts, analytical techniques, internal and external competitor analysis and evaluation of strategic options. This is a core course for MBA.
cilos: Apply theories/frameworks (e.g. SWOT Analysis and Porter’s Five Forces) for in-depth industry analysis, for anticipating and predicting future industry development.
Examine some of the firm's specific underpinnings of competitive advantage and growth in both domestic and international settings.
Evaluate some of the challenges in implementing the strategy that has been formulated.

MGMT 5480.title: Strategic Management in China
MGMT 5480.description: The primary topic of this course is strategic management in the Chinese context.  This course has three major objectives: 1) to help students understand the conditions under which different kinds of strategy have the potential to create economic value and competitive advantage for Chinese context; 2) to help students who plan to work in Chinese companies understand their roles and responsibilities in helping the companies to achieve competitive advantage; and 3)to help those, who work in foreign companies that either already have or will have operations in China, obtain the knowledge necessary to compete or cooperate with companies in Chinese context more successfully.
cilos: Understand the extent to which China is different from other countries and how such differences affect business strategies in the Chinese context.
More accurately assess the opportunities and challenges in setting up business operations in China and to develop corresponding sound business and corporate strategies.
Be better prepared to help multi-national companies to develop sound China strategies in order to compete in the Chinese market more successfully.

MGMT 5490.title: Judgment in Managerial Decision Making
MGMT 5490.description: This is a course with an in-depth discussion on the nature of human thinking and judgment. The overall emphasis of this course will be on illustrating errors and biases in thinking and judgment and their managerial implications. In other words, the class is designed to give students a "rational mind". The concepts we will discuss are key to removing the obstacles in thinking, solving problems, and making decisions. Topics that we will focus on include Common Biases, Experts and Novices, Heuristics, Judgment under Uncertainty, Nonrational Escalation of Commitment, and the Psychology of Delaying Decisions.
cilos: Evaluate the general nature of human thinking and judgment.
Identify the major errors and biases in thinking and judgment.
Recognize the obstacles in problem solving and decision making, and develop an awareness to removing them.
Develop strategies to overcome the obstacles in problem solving and decision making.
Apply the newly learned methodology in managerial contexts.

MGMT 5490.title: Irrational and Rational Thinking and Judgment in Management
MGMT 5490.description: This is a course with an in-depth discussion on the nature of human thinking and judgment.  The overall emphasis of this course will be on illustrating errors and biases in thinking and judgment and their managerial implications.  In other words, the class is designed to give you a "rational mind".  The concepts we will discuss are key to remove the obstacles in thinking, solving problems, and making decisions.  Topics that we will focus on include Common Biases, Experts and Novices, Heuristics, Judgment under Uncertainty, Nonrational Escalation of Commitment, and the Psychology of Delaying Decisions.
cilos: Evaluate the general nature of human thinking and judgment.
Identify the major errors and biases in thinking and judgment.
Recognize the obstacles in problem solving and decision making, and develop an awareness to removing them.
Develop strategies to overcome the obstacles in problem solving and decision making.
Apply the newly learned methodology in managerial contexts.

MGMT 5510.title: Applied Strategic Thinking
MGMT 5510.description: This course will explore the immediate ability to contribute to top management's strategic conversations in students' current organization.  It teaches how to think strategically and provides the opportunity to apply this thinking in a team environment.  Students will be able to immediately apply the thinking and skills learnt to the current job.
cilos: Explain a summarized company strategy.
Apply strategic thinking tools and presepectives to see the future of their industry.
Generate alternative strategies for a business unit.
Construct an implementation plan for business strategy and decision making.

MGMT 5550.title: Effective Negotiations
MGMT 5550.description: This course focuses on two-party negotiations in a wide variety of settings ranging from simple buyer-seller bargains to complex, multiple-issue strategic relationships.
cilos: Develop the ability to compare, contrast, and differentiate among different negotiation situations.
Judge the behavior and motives of individuals and groups in various negotiating situations.
Analyze negotiation situations to identify which effective core negotiating concepts can be applied and modified.
Design and implement strategies for negotiating effectively across a wide range of situations.

MGMT 5570.title: Applied Merger and Acquisition for Corporates
MGMT 5570.description: This course is designed to prepare business managers to succeed as members of a merger and acquisition project team. Students will be able to work out how merger and acquisition can help to achieve the strategy, to know how merger and acquisition transactions work in practice from search to merger integration, to get insight into the particular opportunities and challenges of merger and acquisition, and to apply this thinking in a team environment.
cilos: Appraise how merger and acquisition can help achieve a firm's strategy.
Identify how merger and acquisition transactions work in practice, from initial search through to merger integration.
Recognize nsight into the opportunities and challenges of merger and acquisition in China.
Execute the merger and acquisition thinking in a team environment.

MGMT 5590.title: Responsible Leadership
MGMT 5590.description: Great leaders and corporations take greater responsibilities for its customers, employees, shareholders, and society. This class is to learn what it takes to be a responsible leader and how leaders can create responsible corporations. This course also intends to change behavior for future leaders by teaching decision making framework for making responsible and ethical decisions as they face these challenges. Maybe graded PP. This is a core course for MBA.
cilos: Recognize the differing perspectives of defining and applying ‘responsible leadership’ and ‘ethics’ by exposure to conceptual frameworks from management science (and philosophy) and from ‘everyday discourses’ from business practitioners.

Identify and apply tools, concepts, and theories to perform analyses of the different approaches to responsible leadership and ethics in practice, motives and inspiration (moral, strategic, shareholder, philanthropic, etc.) behind these differences.
Enhance personal development to consider moral reflections on how to respond to ethical dilemmas in a business environment.
Examine practical case studies relating to the applied nature of responsible leadership and ethics in relation to local and global settings and the issues and controversies that surround them.

MGMT 5640.title: Time to Lead
MGMT 5640.description: This course will help students reflect on their learning in the MBA program and prepare them for their leadership roles in the future. Graded P or F.
cilos: Develop skills and competencies that enable effective leadership.
Develop a plan that will enable an immediate and noticeable impact on how they lead at work.
Reconcile skills and competencies at the beginning of the program with skill and competency growth at the end of the program.

MGMT 5670.title: Managing Change
MGMT 5670.description: This course helps you understand your strengths and development areas as a change agent. It then explores a model of change and the role of the change agent as a leader and influencer of others. An online simulation is used to help understand motivation and resistance in recipients of change. Finally, hands on practice is conducted for some key change agent competencies including creating a vision and communication.
cilos: Recognize how personal characteristics impact a person role as change agent and nd deal with resistance in yourself and others.
Define the stages of change and associated challenges of each.
Identify how to  design and facilitate change.
Use the experience in practicing communication and decision skills of a change agent.
Design a personal development plan to improve required skills as a change agent.

MGMT 5750.title: Deal Making across Asia and China
MGMT 5750.description: This course specifically focuses on formulating and applying practical deal-making strategies to real-world transactions in the Asia Pacific region. This is a highly participatory and interactive course instead of purely lecture-style. Participants are asked to play the roles of deal makers -- which role may be as a lead negotiator, investor, investment banker, salesman, consultant, or investment advisor -- in pioneering transactions.
cilos: Define different kinds of transaction structures in the Chinese and Asian contexts.
Identify the different country and cultural contexts in China and Asia.
Compare, contrast, and differentiate between different types of deals and the contexts in which they take place.
Critically analyze a new situation to identify which techniques and contextual factors are the most critical.
Design and implement strategies using the above knowledge in order to structure, negotiate, and close deals in a variety of Chinese and Asian contexts.
Present the deals effectively to potential deal partners and other members of the team.
Tackle ethical challenges conducting deals in China and Asia.

MGMT 5760.title: Management Consulting
MGMT 5760.description: This course is intended for students who are exploring consulting as a career option or who want to be more effective at working out and communicating recommendations. This course will teach students the key skills that management consultants use to solve business problems. This will be a demanding case-based course where students will learn the tools, skills and approaches adopted in leading management consultancies.
cilos: Diagnose the situation of a business problem.
Structure the business problem.
Prove a hypothesis.
Apply relevant frameworks to solve a business problem.
Apply fact-based analytical tools to identify insights.
Design compelling communications to share their thinking.

MGMT 5820.title: Global Leadership and Governance
MGMT 5820.description: This course is designed to inform and inspire MBA students to evolve in their development as global leaders. Drawing from the instructor’s extensive experience in researching, teaching and practicing leadership and governance, students will be provided with actual experiences and lessons learned from the instructor.
cilos: Identify the important characteristics that distinguish a leader from a manager.
Recognize different leadership styles and the limitations that come with them.
Apply relevant leadership principles for effective time management and staff empowerment.

MGMT 5870.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation in FinTech
MGMT 5870.description: This course introduces fundamental concepts relevant for developing FinTech entrepreneurial opportunities. The course begins with frameworks for understanding technology innovation and evolution, and then dives into how new ideas can be generated and assessed, and brought to market by developing an effective organization and relationships in the financial ecosystem.
cilos: Define technology innovation and evolution.
Develop and assess creative FinTech ideas.
Develop the business model for a FinTech innovation.
Develop effective external collaborations in the financial ecosystem.
Building an effective entrepreneurial organization to harness the FinTech ideas.

MGMT 5883.title: Managing Creativity and Innovation
MGMT 5883.description: Creativity is the generation of new and useful ideas. Innovation is the successful implementation of those ideas. Creativity is therefore the foundation of innovation. In a world of accelerating change and fleeting opportunity, creativity and innovation are critical aspects of every manager’s job. This course is designed to help students enhance their creativity, their team’s creativity, the creativity of the people working with them, and ultimately the innovation in their organization. Graded P or F.
cilos: Develop innovation, especially disruptive innovation, in organization.
Identify specific techniques for fostering creativity in themselves, others and innovation in organization.
Assess the enhancement and environment for individual and team creativity.

MGMT 5883.title: Managing Creativity and Innovation
MGMT 5883.description: Creativity is the generation of new and useful ideas. Innovation is the successful implementation of those ideas. Creativity is therefore the foundation of innovation. In a world of accelerating change and fleeting opportunity, creativity and innovation are critical aspects of every manager’s job. This course is designed to help you enhance your creativity, your team’s creativity, the creativity of the people working with you, and ultimately the innovation in your organization.
cilos: Develop innovation, especially disruptive innovation, in organization.
Identify specific techniques for fostering creativity in themselves, others and innovation in organization.
Assess the enhancement and environment for individual and team creativity.

MGMT 5890.title: Principles for Global Leaders
MGMT 5890.description: Through ample case studies, group work and reflection time, the course aims at helping students to enhance their self-awareness, improve their communication skills, build stronger connections and trust with classmates and provide deeper knowledge in the principles of global leadership. This learning has the potential to propel students faster in their leadership career development.
cilos: Solve business problems and develop advanced solution as a leader.
Apply responsible leader skills into business management.
Recognize and identify own core values, goal and interest which determine career success.
Evaluate areas of compatibility and conflict among team members for effective business decision.
Execute leadership to manage a team efficiently.

MGMT 5950.title: Sustainability as a Competitive Advantage
MGMT 5950.description: Sustainability -- or the principles, strategies, and practices that enable organizations to thrive and endure while contributing to g economic growth, social progress, and environmental resilience -- is a megatrend that is transforming companies, markets and societies. As awareness of sustainability rises amongst consumers and across society, the dynamics of industry competition also change. Companies that use the lens of sustainability to drive innovation, create new business models, and shape future markets establish new sources of competitive advantage that could be both financially profitable and socially and environmentally rewarding. This course will provide an understanding of the fundamental aspects of sustainability, both environmentally and socially, as a business issue and how these affect corporate strategy, operations, culture and competitiveness. In particular, the course will examine how these might have shifted, or accelerated, as a result of the Covid-19 pandemic and how business is responding.
cilos: Evaluate the impacts of sustainability   in operations, finance and investment, product and service development and stakeholder relations.
Establish new sources of competitive advantage in future markets.
Engage peers and business leaders effectively.

MGMT 5960.title: Achieving High Performance in Teams
MGMT 5960.description: The course offers a unique opportunity to develop students’ understanding of how to lead and participate in a high performance team as well as address the challenge of virtual teamwork. The course offers a highly unusual and exciting experiential component when students will form small virtual teams to compete in a competitive team performance challenge.
cilos: Recognize the impact of their personalities and behaviour on others.
Evaluate the impact of their cultural values and behaviour on others.
Identify the necessary tools of a feedback culture for team effectiveness.
Plan and navigate a team development journey.
Assess the performance of a team they are leading or a member of the team and introduce changes to improve performance.

MGMT 5970.title: Leading Virtual Teams to High Performance
MGMT 5970.description: Teaming in a virtual environment has never been so widespread. The Covid-19 pandemic was a major catalyst for organizations of all kinds to switch to, invest in and accept virtual team collaboration. What new skills do members of virtual teams need to master to achieve effective collaboration and high performance? How has operating remotely and through video impacted group dynamics and interpersonal behavior? Whether the students are leaders or members of a team, in this course they will deepen their understanding of teaming and master the latest skills needed to take virtual teams to high performance. The students will also have opportunities to engage in virtual teaming, both collaboratively and competitively, with their fellow class participants and in a new simulation in which teams compete on a voyage in outer space. Graded P or F.
cilos: Lead teams operating in a virtual environment more effectively.
Contribute more constructively to a team operating in a virtual environment.
Empower a team more successfully to strive for high performance.
Understand how to address hurdles encountered by team operating in virtual environments.
Leverage real virtual team experiences from simulations in the course to learn how to improve their virtual teaming capabilities.

MGMT 5971.title: Innovating via Entrepreneurship and Intrapreneurship
MGMT 5971.description: This course focuses on the essence of innovation, which is relevant to both entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship in startups, large corporations, or family businesses. Throughout the course, students will gain self-insight and learn practical tools for innovation as they create a business plan, project proposal, or new business line to present to a panel of experienced innovators.
cilos: Recognize personal values, passions and purpose to decide between entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship.
Evaluate project and venture viability.
Develop and pitch a business case.
Apply the skills to pitch project and venture proposals to key stakeholders.

MGMT 5972.title: Interpersonal Dynamics, Networking and the Art of Influencing Business Leaders
MGMT 5972.description: The course focuses on effective client relationships for students pursuing advisory roles. The curriculum will concentrate on day-to-day client relationship practices, equipping students to become competent professionals. To enhance student learning, the course will also outline specific strategies for applying these insights during internships or entry-level positions after graduation. Graded P or F.
cilos: Classify the key debates between different approaches to influencing executives.
Assess personal networking patterns and identify options to improve the ability to network.
Recognize the process of selling and implications for influence in other situations.
Develop their approach to networking, collaborating with others, and influencing executives.

MGMT 5980.title: Managerial Decision Making
MGMT 5980.description: Successful organizations excel by the quality of their offerings and services in the market place. Internally, leaders and managers distinguish themselves by the quality of their decisions. As leaders and managers, you will find that your decision making ability is tested and challenged at work every day. Your ability to make quality decisions will determine your long term professional success and the success of your organization. Quality management decisions do not need to be hit and miss, nor should they be based on titles and ranks. Quality decision making is a competence that can be acquired and a discipline that should be practiced.
cilos: Identify approaches to lead team(s) in making the best decisions to achieve organizational goals.
Apply a decision making framework, tested by many practical situations, hence approach any decision with confidence.
Articulate, defend, and successfully implement the decisions made.
Recognize the most effective leadership styles in leading the team to make the best decisions.

MGMT 5981.title: Corporate Innovation and Growth
MGMT 5981.description: The course will share cutting edge best practices of building high performing innovative companies. It will help students to understand how to strategically arrange innovation activities to ensure a company’s robust short-term performance and healthy long-term growth, how to design proper funding and accountability structures to nurture and discipline various innovation and growth projects, how to initiate and execute innovation programs to deliver expected results and how to build holistic innovative engines to sustain long-term development. Graded P or F.
cilos: Execute innovation activities strategically to ensure a company’s robust short-term performance and healthy long-term growth.
Design proper funding and accountability structures to nurture and discipline various innovation and growth projects.
Construct holistic innovative engines to sustain long-term development.
Develop hands-on knowledge and tools on setting up and executing performance driven innovation systems in established companies.
Apply the tools/frameworks to tackle various innovation challenges in corporate innovation.

MGMT 5982.title: Cross-cultural Negotiation
MGMT 5982.description: This course aims to broaden students’ understanding in negotiation and dispute resolution. It enhances students’ ability to analyze the kinds of conflict and negotiation situations that they would be involved in, and to derive optimal strategies that help attain their goal in these situations. This course extends the negotiation repertoire from interpersonal to intercultural level. We will discuss how culture affects negotiation and dispute resolution effectiveness.
cilos: Identify systematic frameworks and models of negotiation in cross-cultural level.
Apply knowledge of conflict management which involves cultural issues.
Analyze different types of conflict and negotiation.
Develop negotiation skills.
Plan optimal negotiation strategies to attain the most favorable outcome.

MGMT 5983.title: Introduction to Management
MGMT 5983.description: This course provides an accelerated overview of the materials covered in undergraduate classes in management and strategy, aimed at postgraduate students with no undergraduate background in business. It will cover essential frameworks in both organizational behavior (leadership and motivation, organizational culture and design) and strategy (business and corporate strategy, international business). It also provides an introduction to the case method.

MGMT 5984.title: Strategy Consulting Analytics and Operations Consulting Analytics
MGMT 5984.description: This course gives students the opportunity to practice the skills learned in  the previous courses on real-world projects sourced from real-world clients. In this course, students will focus on recommending a solution to a business problem. Later, in MGMT 6985 Strategic Analytics Implementation, students will focus on implementing this solution.
cilos: Apply consulting techniques in a corporate environment, working with client-side executives, technologists, and data scientists to deliver the right solutions for the right problems.
Apply technical knowledge within a business environment to solve real problems.
Match specific technologies and analytical tools to specific problems faced by specific clients.

Analyze the strategic and operational impacts of specific technologies and analytical tools within specific client environments, especially given the configuration of the operational processes involved.
Understand client-side stakeholder needs to manage the project and impact how the results will be received by the clients.

MGMT 5985.title: Strategic Analytics Implementation
MGMT 5985.description: This course continues the real-world projects initiated in MGMT 5984 Strategy Consulting Analytics and Operations Consulting Analytics, focusing on implementing the solution to the business case recommended during MGMT 5984.
cilos: Apply operational consulting techniques in a corporate environment, working with client-side executives, technologists, and data scientists to implement a technical solution within the context of client-side processes.
Leverage statistical analyses and machine learning algorithms in a corporate data environment, working with client-side personnel to obtain access to data and analysis platforms.
Quickly and efficiently prototype and refine technical solutions via code reuse and API-based access to publicly available tools.
Understand client-side stakeholder needs to manage the project and impact how the results will be received by the clients.

MGMT 5986.title: Digital Transformation in the Exponential Age
MGMT 5986.description: Reinvention is at the core of transformation, leveraging digital technology as a force multiplier. In this course, the instructor provides practical tips, approaches, methodology, and frameworks to address the challenges that students will be called upon to deliver at some point in their careers. Graded P or F.
cilos: Explain the underlying principles, basic concepts, and methodology around Digital Transformation strategy and execution.
Summarize the common approaches, organizational design options, transformation frameworks, change theory, and leadership techniques for transformation.
Recognize the limits of theory and gain an understanding of the common pitfalls and tradeoffs when theory is applied in practice for Digital Transformation.
Recognize how to leverage and apply technology in real life environments and use cases.
Use techniques to overcome organizational resistance, inertia, and other structural and nonstructural obstacles.
Apply the skills to implement and drive transformation in their own organizations.

MGMT 5987.title: AI, Innovation, and Product Management
MGMT 5987.description: This course provides the basic principles and tools that business managers need to ensure outcomes align with business needs. Students will gain an industry insider’s view that goes beyond theory to cover actionable guidelines, practical tips, and best practices. By examining the differing modes of product development in Silicon Valley and China, this course provides a new framework and approach for competition and innovation in the Age of AI. Graded P or F.
cilos: Explain the basic concepts, use cases, applications, and limitations of artificial intelligence.
Apply the skills to leverage AI to capture market opportunities and address operational needs.
Explain the basic methodology, tools, and concepts of product management, including how to build AI into a company’s products and services.
Develop product strategy at both the corporate and startup level.
Differentiate the different modes of innovation and AI between the East and West.

MGMT 5988.title: Effective People Decisions and Career Management: Unlocking Talent and Personal Success
MGMT 5988.description: This course is designed to empower MBA students with the skills and insights needed to make impactful people decisions and maximize their full career potential. By delving into the art and science of making smart people decisions, students will learn how to recruit the right talents for the right roles in order to build high-performing teams, nurture individual potential, and drive organizational success. Through interactive discussions, real-world case studies, and fun exercises, students will gain the confidence and expertise to define talent gaps, needs, screen, attract, retain and develop the right people on their teams.
cilos: Understand the impact of people decisions on performance, teams, and career success.
Apply effective methods to identify talent needs and hire the right people.
Manage workplace relationships and collaborate effectively in complex organizations.
Develop a flexible, values-based career plan and navigate career changes confidently.

MGMT 5990.title: Consequential Communication for Business Leader
MGMT 5990.description: One of the must learn to be a successful effective leader is to communicate consequentially internally and externally. This course provides students chance to enhance skills including summarization, elaboration and Question and Answer, through different modes of communications like One-to-many speeches and presentation and Many-to-many meetings and discussions. Graded P or F.
cilos: Construct and organize consequential communication.
Deliver consequential communication efficiently and effectively.
Evaluate self and other’s communications.
Recommend useful feedback for individual and team communication.
Develop continuous improvement plan for consequential communication.

MGMT 5990.title: Consequential Communication for Business Leader
MGMT 5990.description: One of the must learn to be a successful effective leader is to communicate consequentially internally and externally. This course provides students chance to enhance skills including summarization, elaboration and Question and Answer, through different modes of communications like One-to-many speeches and presentation and Many-to-many meetings and discussions. Graded P or F.
cilos: Construct and organize consequential communication.
Deliver consequential communication efficiently and effectively.
Evaluate self and other’s communications.
Recommend useful feedback for individual and team communication.
Develop continuous improvement plan for consequential communication.

MGMT 5991.title: Agile Leadership in the Digital Age
MGMT 5991.description: This course explores how organizations navigate exponential disruptions through transformation journeys such as digitalization, market expansion, agile teamwork, innovation leadership, and ESG strategy implementation. It spans industries including banking, global industrials, family business, media, social commerce, and fast fashion across global and Asian contexts. Students will develop strong mental frameworks, practical tools, and opportunities for cross‑learning to navigate rapid change.
cilos: Apply sensemaking frameworks to interpret and respond to exponential disruptions.
Demonstrate curiosity-driven leadership to foster innovation and adaptability.
Strengthen self-awareness to develop an authentic and engaging leadership style.
Design and implement agile strategies for business model transformation in diverse contexts.

MGMT 5992.title: Communication for Business Leaders
MGMT 5992.description: In order to be an effective leader, one must learn to communicate effectively and consequently. This course will focus on effective leadership through effective and consequential communication. Whether leaders are effective largely depends on how effectively leaders communicate. Immediate feedback for continuous improvements will be given by peers and the instructor during the class and in breakout sessions. Graded P or F.
cilos: Identify how effective communication supports and strengthens a leader’s effectiveness in a business environment.
Summarize the key points using the golden rules of responsible business leadership as a guide.
Evaluate potential crisis outcomes and apply effective solutions to practical business scenarios.

MGMT 6300.title: Special Topics in Human Resources Management
MGMT 6300.description: Advanced topics of current interest in human resources management.
cilos: Analyze and evaluate the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.

MGMT 6400.title: Special Topics in Organizational Behavior
MGMT 6400.description: Advanced topics of current interest in organizational behavior.
cilos: Analyze and evaluate the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.

MGMT 6500-6590.title: Special Topics in Management
MGMT 6500-6590.description: Advanced topics of current interest in Management.
cilos: Analyze and evaluate the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.
Develop hands-on research skills.
Advance their own research agendas such as papers targeted for submission to top tier management journals.

MGMT 6970.title: Independent Study
MGMT 6970.description: Study of selected issues in organizational management under the supervision of a faculty member. (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)
cilos: Examine a specific topic in Management.
Read academic articles critically.
Write academic articles effectively.

MGMT 6990.title: MPhil Thesis Research
MGMT 6990.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member. A successful defense of the thesis leads to Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in management studies.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

MGMT 7100.title: Behavioral Science
MGMT 7100.description: In-depth study of the foundations of behavioral science research using examples from organizational behavior and other related business disciplines.
cilos: Recognize the philosophical development of behavioral science (Part 1).
Understand the trend and predicted future of behavioral science.
Know the position of past and current management research under the history and tend of behavior science.
Seek new directions of management research by knowing the past and current positions.

MGMT 7120.title: Doctoral Seminar in Management
MGMT 7120.description: Presentations and discussions of current research topics in Organizational Behavior and Human Resources Management for doctoral students.
cilos: Make use of up-to-date and in-depth knowledge about management research in general and organizational behavior in particular, providing them with the foundation to conduct independent substantive scholarly research.
Demonstrate an in depth understanding of contemporary issues in organizational behaviors.
Perform different aspects of the role of faculty in academia, such as conducting research, writing research reviews.

MGMT 7130.title: Doctoral Seminar in Organization Theory and Strategy
MGMT 7130.description: Presentations and discussions of current research topics in organization theory and strategic management for doctoral students.
cilos: Demonstrate a sound grasp of the literature in their specialization.
Apply their specialized knowledge to solve related business problems in an innovative fashion.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of core business functions.
Integrate functional knowledge to solve business problems within their area of specialization.
Teach independent courses or lead lab/tutorial sessions effectively.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

MGMT 7140.title: Doctoral Seminar in Behavioral Research Methods
MGMT 7140.description: Presentations and discussions of current research topics in Behavioral Research Methods for doctoral students.
cilos: Recognize common research methods and techniques used in behavioral research.
Understand how these methods were used by researchers to address important research questions.
Develop hand-on knowledge on statistical packages.

MGMT 7160.title: Doctoral Seminar: Frontiers in Strategy Research
MGMT 7160.description: This course is designed as a doctoral seminar discussion that provides an overview of some of the most contemporary research topics in strategic management. We will survey a select set of strategy topics including ESG and sustainability, global strategy, corporate governance, innovation models, digital economy, mergers and acquisitions, and global value chains. Through in-depth and in-class discussion of some of the cutting-edge research in the field of strategic management, we focus on developing ideas for a research proposal in terms of theory development and research design.
cilos: Conduct in-depth discussions of selected research papers to have a good understanding of major theories in the field of strategic management and international business.
Work closely on the development of ideas for a research proposal.

MGMT 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
MGMT 7990.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in management studies.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
